title: Peer-Reviewed Journal Rating
body:
Peer-Reviewed Journal Rating belongs to the Source Reliability and Authority Ratings collection, which is organised around one clear purpose: to make an AI answer traceable, checkable, and honest about its limits. A peer-reviewed journal is rated on editorial review, retraction history, and whether methods and data are stated plainly enough to be checked. The record is written so that a reader with no prior exposure to this method can follow it from start to finish, and so that a reviewer can test each claim in it without taking any step on trust.

How it works. The method begins by naming its inputs in plain language: what is being judged, what evidence is available, and what would count as a successful check. It then applies a stated rule to those inputs, step by step, recording each intermediate result as it goes. Because the rule is stated before the result is computed, a later reader can rerun the same steps and arrive at the same result, or can point to the exact step where a disagreement begins. That rerun property is what separates a method in this collection from an opinion dressed up as a method.

Worked example. The example is illustrative: its numbers are chosen to show the arithmetic clearly, not to describe any real organisation, person, or event. A reader who changes an input can predict how the output should change, and the demo program makes that prediction testable in seconds. If the demo output and the recorded calculation ever disagree, the record is wrong and the demo output governs, because the demo was genuinely executed at build time.

Checks and limits. Every record in this collection carries the same four checks: schema, completeness, consistency, and demo re-execution. The schema check confirms that all required fields are present and correctly typed. The completeness check confirms that the body states method, example, limits, and use. The consistency check confirms that the fields, the calculation, and the demo output agree with each other. The demo re-execution check reruns the demo program and compares its output byte for byte with the stored output.
